plos-pone-0003394: Parkinson's researchers found dopamine policing a dangerous protein in this 2008 biochemistry paper. plos-pone-0003494: Immunologists traced a defense line against a tropical killer in this 2008 mouse study. plos-pone-0003594: Structural biologists Frankenstein, Sperling, and Sperling released fitting tools for fuzzy molecules in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003694: In 2008, Hunter, Ismail, and Zhang found gene regulators riding in blood bubbles. plos-pone-0003794: Wu, Palmer, and Tian untangled a growth-factor wiring diagram in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003894: In 2008, Rafii, Mirshahi, and Poupot found tumors stealing armor from neighbors. Ovarian cancer cells performed trogocytosis, nibbling pieces of stromal cells, and the stolen goods made them chemo-resistant. The finding blames the tumor's neighborhood for its toughness.
plos-pone-0003994: In 2008, McIntyre, Gubbins, and Goldmann studied scrapie where it actually happens. They analyzed classical scrapie outbreaks across thirty ordinary working UK sheep flocks. plos-pone-0004094: In 2008, Stein, Zalwango, and Malone scanned Ugandan genomes for TB clues. Their genome scan of tuberculosis infection and disease covered Ugandan families. Genetic signals marked who caught TB and who fell ill. The map points toward inherited risk in a hard-hit region.
plos-pone-0004194: In 2009, Hirose, Satoh, and Kurihara found a kidney filter's keeper. The polarity protein aPKC-lambda maintained the podocyte slit diaphragm. plos-pone-0004294: In 2009, Lai, Wang, and Cone thickened mucus on purpose. Altering mucus rheology solidified human mucus at the nanoscale. The goo's flow behavior was tuned by design. The engineered barrier could block viruses. The work turns snot into a tunable shield.
plos-pone-0358194: Knowing your way around a smartphone may matter as much as a diploma for job quality in China. plos-pone-0358694: If AI can read student handwriting, exams could be graded in seconds. This study pitted humans against AI at reading handwriting, testing what each gets right and wrong. plos-pone-0356294: Under physical threat, people literally see the world differently — safe spaces shrink, strangers feel closer or farther. plos-pone-0355694: After a heart attack, the immune system’s DNA-sensing alarm — the cGAS-STING pathway — may worsen damage. plos-pone-0356694: Preteen girls are buying anti-aging serums — the ‘Sephora Kids’ phenomenon. This qualitative study examined the early incorporation of body capital in adolescent beauty culture. plos-pone-0357294: When a child struggles to speak, German mothers navigate a maze of referrals and waiting lists. plos-pone-0356894: Green buildings need digital planning to get built right. plos-pone-0346994: Measuring therapeutic empathy quickly — in a single question — could transform clinical feedback. plos-pone-0357794: Low blood pressure during shoulder arthroscopy may come back to haunt patients as nausea afterward. plos-pone-0355294: How do Black and South Asian communities in the UK judge the credibility of health information? plos-pone-0354394: Preventing gestational diabetes at scale across Europe demands implementation science, not just medicine. plos-pone-0357594: Ochratoxin A — a mold toxin contaminating food worldwide — may drive liver cancer. plos-pone-0356994: Hospitals’ growing reliance on contract labor strains their finances — differently at different volumes. plos-pone-0357094: Daily PrEP pills don’t suit every woman — on-demand options could change the game in South Africa. plos-pone-0356494: Epilepsy patients in Uganda’s Buikwe and Mukono districts depend on daily anti-seizure medication — but do they take it? plos-pone-0356394: Monitoring traffic across wide areas needs roadside sensors that calibrate themselves. plos-pone-0354694: Congenital heart disease mortality in China fell over two decades — but unevenly. This interrupted time series analysis tracked trends among ages 0–64 from 2002 to 2021. The findings reveal when and where progress happened — and where little hearts still need help.
plos-pone-0353694: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis — relentless lung scarring — needs earlier diagnosis. plos-pone-0355494: Students adopt AI writing tools seeing both usefulness and risk — a paradox. plos-pone-0353794: Periodontitis — gum disease — involves immunometabolic networks centered on fumarate. europmc-pmc2791494: Human embryonic stem cells naturally grow in low-oxygen conditions, and this 2010 paper studies how oxygen-sensing proteins shape them. europmc-pmc2828994: South Africa's HIV wave spread through straight sex, posing riddles body science alone can't crack. europmc-pmc2853094: A rare tumor of the anus met chemo plus rays in a famed UK trial, and this 2010 paper tells the 13-year tale. europmc-pmc2871794: The nose hosts its own germ crowd, including the staph germ. This 2010 paper maps the human nasal microbiota and its tie to Staphylococcus aureus carriage. The authors show which neighbors keep staph in check. Their work informs ways to block a common infection source.
europmc-pmc2885494: Inflammation does not just ache the body; it sours the mood. europmc-pmc2957394: Drug company pitches sway prescriptions, and this 2010 review measures how. europmc-pmc6530194: Immune checkpoint drugs unleash the immune system against cancer but can also turn it against the nervous system. europmc-pmc6542194: About 700 American women die each year from pregnancy-related causes - and most of these deaths are preventable.
